DS-01.name: The twins that aren't
DS-01.orient: Two bright white stars were logged as twins because they look alike in the eyepiece. Appearance is a starting observation, not identity.
DS-01.notice: Look at both targets. Read the inherited log. If the eyepiece is not enough, the basin still has a known light south of the dome.
DS-01.reason: A spectrum is a record of structure in the light. Two objects can look the same and still leave different traces.
DS-01.teach: Visible color and brightness do not prove two stars are the same kind. A known lamp gives a repeatable pattern you can compare against stellar traces.
DS-01.scaffold: Walk to Lamp Bench for a fair reference, then bring that pattern back to the plate spectrograph. Try to align the two stellar traces. Log what refuses to match.
explainMore: Looking the same from far away does not prove much. I should know.
The lamp is not a lecture. It is a light you can test because you already know the source.

misconceptions.eyepiece-twins: If they look white and bright, they still might not be the same light. The traces have to agree.
misconceptions.spectrum-quiz: This is not a vocabulary match. You are comparing patterns you recorded.

DS-01.worldCue: The dome wash is the problem. The lamp is south of here, on purpose.

DS-02.name: The cooler ember
DS-02.orient: The old notes treat a reddish star as an ember, like a hot coal. Color folklore is not a temperature measurement.
DS-02.notice: Compare the reddish target with a white one you already logged. Watch where each trace is brightest, not only the color you saw.
DS-02.reason: A peak sitting farther toward longer wavelength is not evidence that the source is hotter.
DS-02.teach: Visible redness is one observation. Peak position is another. Temperature inference has to follow the evidence you actually marked.
DS-02.scaffold: Slide the peak marker to each trace's brightest place. Use the wavelength marks, not color memory.
explainMore: Fire-color folklore is stubborn. The trace does not care what a coal looks like.
I will not invent a temperature you did not measure.

misconceptions.red-hotter: Red as fire is a story. Peak position is the evidence on this bench.
misconceptions.color-only: Color without a peak mark is not enough here.

DS-02.worldCue: The reddish target is still in the same sky. The spectrograph can hold both traces.

DS-03.name: Two cairns
DS-03.orient: Two stars can look about equally bright and still not sit at the same distance.
DS-03.notice: Walk the west rim, then the east. Compare the season plates from both ends of the baseline.
DS-03.reason: A nearby star shifts against the background when you change viewpoint. A distant one barely moves. Brightness does not decide that.
DS-03.teach: Apparent brightness is not a distance rule. Geometry on walked plates is the evidence here.
DS-03.scaffold: Stand at both cairns. Switch plate A and plate B. Mark the star that actually reverses with the baseline.
explainMore: The star did not jump. You moved.
Equal look is not equal distance.

misconceptions.brighter-closer: Brighter is not automatically closer. These two already look similarly bright.
misconceptions.star-jumped: The shift is the baseline, not the star leaping.

DS-03.worldCue: West cairn, then east cairn. The walk is the instrument.

DS-04.name: Unlabeled plot
DS-04.orient: The board has no legend on purpose. You are building a diagram from measurements, not labeling a poster.
DS-04.notice: Use the peaks you marked and the distance rank from the cairns. Place those stars on empty axes.
DS-04.reason: A pattern can appear after points are placed. Naming the regions comes after that, not before.
DS-04.teach: This is not a hunt for memorized diagram parts. The points have to come from your notes.
DS-04.scaffold: Place the hot white star, the cooler ember, and the intrinsically brighter far cairn star where your evidence puts them.
explainMore: If the poster already had the answer, we would not need the basin.
I will not place the points for you.

misconceptions.poster-hr: A finished diagram with labels to identify is the wrong job.
misconceptions.swapped-axes: Shorter-wavelength peak sits toward the hotter side of this board.

DS-04.worldCue: The unlabeled board is at the station, not in a textbook.

DS-05.name: Not one life
DS-05.orient: Stars do not all follow one cartoon lifecycle. Initial mass changes the path.
DS-05.notice: Compare the hotter massive star with the cooler sun-like one. Then check the remnant plate.
DS-05.reason: A massive star can end in a remnant after a violent late stage. A sun-like star will not explode as a supernova.
DS-05.teach: Mass branches lives. Gravity does not make a star 'burn' by squeezing a campfire.
DS-05.scaffold: Pick a future for each star, then match the outburst remnant to the massive branch.
explainMore: Every-star-supernova is a storybook.
The remnant plate has to match the branch, not the wall cartoon.

misconceptions.all-supernova: Not every star becomes a supernova.
misconceptions.gravity-burns: Gravity holds a star together. It is not a fire starter.

DS-05.worldCue: The remnant plate is at the spectrograph after you have a branch to test.

DS-06.name: What the floor is made of
DS-06.orient: The rock in your hand has a cosmic history. That does not mean every element was made in a star.
DS-06.notice: Pick up the Quiet Floor stone. Compare a metal-poor trace with a metal-rich one.
DS-06.reason: Hydrogen and helium mostly come from the early universe. Many heavier elements need stellar processes, and some of the heaviest need explosions or neutron-star events.
DS-06.teach: Do not stamp 'everything was made in stars.' The missing metal lines in the poor star are the evidence that later generations added metals.
DS-06.scaffold: Walk down to the pan, take the rock, then mark a metal line present in one stellar trace and nearly absent in the other.
explainMore: The stone is ordinary. Its ingredients are not local gossip.
Big Bang nucleosynthesis is not a star factory for iron.

misconceptions.all-in-stars: Not all elements were made in stars. Light elements have an earlier chapter.
misconceptions.all-at-start: The metals were not all present equally at the beginning.

DS-06.worldCue: Quiet Floor first. The spectrograph cannot pick up the rock for you.

DS-07.name: Lines that moved
DS-07.orient: Redshift is a moved pattern, not a red-colored object.
DS-07.notice: The galaxy plates use the same rest lines you already know. See whether the whole pattern has slid.
DS-07.reason: If known lines sit at longer wavelength together, that is a shift of the pattern. A red star is a different claim.
DS-07.teach: Farther plates in this set show larger shifts. One competing story — that every plate shifts the same — fails the farthest plate.
DS-07.scaffold: Align a galaxy trace to the rest marks, then place shift against distance rank for all three plates.
explainMore: A red star can still have unshifted lines. Color is not redshift.
I will not invent a recession speed you did not plot.

misconceptions.redshift-is-red: Redshift is not 'the galaxy looks red.'
misconceptions.same-shift: The plates do not all move by the same amount.

DS-07.worldCue: Galaxy plates live on the plate desk after the floor work.

DS-08.name: Three lines, no label
DS-08.orient: A famous name is not a case. You need more than one independent line of evidence.
DS-08.notice: You already have expansion in the plates and abundance in the metal/rock work. Test the leftover glow with the horn.
DS-08.reason: Pointing at the station wall is noisy. Pointing overhead is quieter. That leftover sky is a third line, still not a slogan.
DS-08.teach: Hot-dense-early history is an inference from converging evidence. One noisy line stays weak by itself. The Big Bang was not a firecracker in empty space.
DS-08.scaffold: On the Quiet Floor, point the horn zenith, wall, and horizon. Pin expansion, leftover glow, and abundance together.
explainMore: I will not let a label replace the clipboard.
If one line is noisy, say so.

misconceptions.name-replaces-evidence: Saying the famous name is not the same as assembling the evidence.
misconceptions.explosion-in-space: An explosion in already-existing space is the wrong picture.

DS-08.worldCue: The horn only works on the quiet pan, away from station lights.

DS-09.name: Not tonight
DS-09.orient: A telescope sees light that already left. Farther can mean earlier.
DS-09.notice: The poster says the distant outburst is happening now. Check a nearby variable later tonight, then look at the distant plate again.
DS-09.reason: The nearby star can change on a human timescale. The distant event's light left long before tonight. We do not know what is happening there right now.
DS-09.teach: A light-year is a distance, not a duration you wait. Lookback is why the poster overclaims.
DS-09.scaffold: Use later tonight at the eyepiece. Log that the nearby target changed and the distant one did not authorize a present-tense caption.
explainMore: I will not describe the current state of a galaxy we cannot see live.
Happening now is a claim the plate does not support.

misconceptions.seeing-now: We are not seeing that distant event right now.
misconceptions.light-year-time: A light-year is how far light travels in a year, not a kind of clock you set.

DS-09.worldCue: Poster at the station, then the eyepiece for later tonight.

DS-10.name: The unlabeled envelope
DS-10.orient: Wren is not asking for a complete story. Say what the light shows, what you can infer, and what you refuse.
DS-10.notice: The envelope has a trace and a peak. It does not have a famous name, a distance, or a live weather report.
DS-10.reason: Observed is the trace. Inferred has to ride on evidence. Unknown stays unknown. Overclaim fails.
DS-10.teach: Honesty about incomplete evidence is the skill. Invented magnitudes and present-tense distant weather are overclaims.
DS-10.scaffold: Sort the unlabeled target into observed, inferred, unknown, and at least one sentence you will not say.
explainMore: I will not name an object you did not identify.
Stopping is part of the science.

misconceptions.completeness-theater: A tidy complete biography is not in the envelope.
misconceptions.naming-is-understanding: A nickname is not a measurement.

DS-10.worldCue: The unlabeled envelope is at the plate desk when the rest of the basin is in the tablet.
